audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition breaks the earnings-to-bridge perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $426 million net cash purchase price; total valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor excludes In-Situ owner earnings and maintenance reinvestment, while the current bridge reflects post-acquisition cash, debt and liabilities; equity-level OE also omits interest attributable to post-2025 financing.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 22, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of In-Situ, Inc. (“In-Situ”), for a cash purchase price of approximately $427 million, net of cash acquired.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possible risk. The $426 million purchase price equals 44.7% of the $952.4 million OE anchor and 2.7% of BASE equity value. Omitted In-Situ earnings understate value, while unreconciled acquisition funding, incremental interest and liabilities can overstate it. The net effect cannot be established from the supplied record and is large enough to invalidate the current same-perimeter valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Construct same-date pro forma OE including In-Situ operating earnings, maintenance reinvestment, integration and purchase-accounting items, and incremental after-tax interest; reconcile the $426 million cash payment and assumed liabilities to July 2026 cash and debt, then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain-tax liabilities may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $116 million net amount ($175 million gross tax benefits, adjusted for $85 million of indirect benefits and $28 million of interest and penalties)
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unindemnified liability for past-period taxes should reduce the equity bridge because its settlement is not a recurring forecast OE expense.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, tax benefits totaled $ 175 million ($ 116 million, net of the impact of $ 85 million of indirect tax benefits offset by $ 28 million associated with potential interest and penalties).
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the entire amount is an incremental claim remains unresolved because Danaher indemnification and balance-sheet recognition must be traced. Even deducting the filed $116 million net amount would reduce BASE value by only about $0.46 per share, or 0.75% of $15.5 billion BASE equity value, compared with the $34.38 per-share gap between BASE value and market price. The gross $175 million would be about $0.70 per share and likewise would not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 2026 recognized liability to Joint versus Separate filings, indirect benefits, accrued interest and penalties, and the Danaher tax-indemnification asset; deduct only the unabsorbed net claim and confirm no double counting in OE.

audit_findings.title: The 2023 trend input is not fully standalone
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially non-standalone corporate costs and financing expense alter 2023 OE and therefore the log-trend anchor used for every growth scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2023 Combined Financial Statements may not be indicative of results had the Company been a separate stand-alone entity throughout the periods presented, nor are the results stated herein indicative of what the Company’s financial position, results of operations and cash flows may be in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that 2023 is a carve-out period, but it does not demonstrate the correct standalone OE adjustment or its net direction. Simply excluding 2023 would raise the anchor from $952.4 million to no more than the $960.3 million latest-actual cap, a $7.9 million change corresponding to about $111 million or $0.44 per share in BASE. That mechanical test is not a substitute for a recast, because the allocated costs and missing financing burden have not been quantified.
audit_findings.action: Recast 2023 with standalone corporate costs and a full-year financing burden, then rerun the log trend; also present the 2024–2025-only capped-anchor sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: A discrete tax benefit remains in the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $21 million FY2025 net discrete tax benefit; one-for-one BASE sensitivity approximately $295 million or $1.18 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit increases FY2025 OE and consequently the trend anchor that is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The net discrete tax benefit related primarily to the reduction of the tax indemnification related to the Separation, excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation and a release of a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The $21 million benefit is filed and its inclusion is a demonstrated normalization issue. Even conservatively treating the entire amount as a one-for-one anchor overstatement would reduce BASE value by about $295 million, or $1.18 per share—approximately 1.9% of BASE value and far short of the $34.38 per-share gap to market price. The actual trend effect should be smaller than this direct sensitivity.
audit_findings.action: Break the $21 million into indemnification, stock-compensation and valuation-allowance components; remove the portions that cannot reasonably recur and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded deferred compensation is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $52 million liability; approximately $0.21 per share if fully deducted
audit_findings.mechanism: The existing unfunded obligation is a claim for compensation already expensed, so settlement will consume cash without reducing future forecast earnings again and should therefore enter the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: All amounts deferred under such plans are unfunded, unsecured obligations and are presented as a component of the compensation and benefits accrual included in other long-term liabilities in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The July 2026 filing demonstrates a $52 million unfunded liability. A full bridge deduction would reduce BASE equity value by only 0.34%, or about $0.21 per share, compared with the $34.38 per-share gap between BASE value and market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the July 2026 $52 million balance has no separately added matching asset or other bridge offset, then deduct the verified net unfunded amount in the next rerun.
